prompt: Which header is normally replaced at each routed Ethernet hop?
explanation: Application data is carried by TCP segments or UDP datagrams, then IP packets, then link-layer frames. Routers replace link-layer headers at each routed hop; IP addresses normally persist absent NAT. TCP ports identify endpoints, not physical interfaces. TLS does not fit perfectly into one OSI layer.

prompt: Which storage architecture normally presents block devices to hosts?
explanation: Switches learn source MAC addresses and forward frames; routers choose IP routes. A stateful firewall tracks connections; IDS alerts while IPS can block. NAS exposes file shares; SAN exposes block storage. Load balancers distribute requests and proxies mediate connections.

prompt: Which service model lets you manage the guest OS on a rented VM?
explanation: IaaS exposes virtual infrastructure, PaaS manages the runtime, SaaS delivers an application. A virtual private cloud isolates logical networks; route tables and security rules control connectivity. Public, private and hybrid deployment models differ from service models.

prompt: A DNS response is truncated over UDP. Which transport can the client retry on port 53?
explanation: TCP provides ordered reliable delivery; UDP does not guarantee delivery. DNS uses UDP and TCP 53; DHCPv4 uses UDP 67/68; SSH and SFTP use TCP 22; HTTPS commonly uses TCP 443 or UDP 443 for HTTP/3. ICMP and GRE use IP protocol numbers rather than transport ports.

prompt: Which medium is immune to electromagnetic interference along its transmission path?
explanation: Copper Ethernet uses electrical signaling; fiber uses light. Single-mode fiber supports long distances; multimode commonly serves shorter links. Match transceiver wavelength, fiber type and link budget. DAC is useful for short rack connections. T568A and T568B specify pair placement.

prompt: Which architecture connects each leaf switch to every spine switch?
explanation: Star networks centralize connections; mesh provides multiple paths. Spine-leaf designs connect each leaf to each spine to provide predictable east-west paths. Three-tier campus designs separate access, distribution and core. Point-to-point links join two endpoints.

prompt: What is the network address of 192.168.10.77/26?
explanation: IPv4 uses 32 bits. A /26 leaves six host bits: 64 addresses and normally 62 usable hosts. Network boundaries increment by 64 in the final octet. RFC1918 ranges are 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16; 169.254/16 is link-local. Longest prefix matching determines route specificity.

prompt: Which technology uses a VNI to identify an overlay segment?
explanation: SDN separates control decisions from forwarding; VXLAN encapsulates Layer 2 over Layer 3. Zero trust evaluates access explicitly; SASE combines network and security services. Infrastructure as code makes configuration repeatable. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, NDP and typically /64 LAN prefixes; dual stack runs both IP versions.

prompt: A /24 and /28 both match a destination. Which route wins first?
options: Lowest hop count regardless of prefix
explanation: Routers choose longest matching prefixes before comparing route preferences for identical prefixes. OSPF is link-state, BGP is path-vector, EIGRP is advanced distance-vector. NAT changes addresses; PAT multiplexes flows using ports. A floating static route has a less preferred administrative distance.

prompt: Which protocol negotiates an Ethernet link aggregation group?
explanation: Access ports normally carry one VLAN; trunks carry multiple VLANs using 802.1Q tags. STP prevents Layer 2 loops; LACP negotiates link aggregation. A Layer 3 interface or router is needed to route between VLANs. MTU mismatch can impair traffic.

prompt: Which action best addresses overlapping-channel interference?
explanation: Wi-Fi shares radio airtime. Channel width, interference, signal strength and client density affect performance. WPA3 provides modern authentication and encryption options; enterprise authentication commonly uses 802.1X. A site survey helps determine coverage and channel reuse.

prompt: Which device supplies temporary power during an outage?
explanation: Plan rack space, power, cooling, grounding, cable paths and physical access. UPS supplies temporary power; PDU distributes power. Label both cable ends and document patch-panel mappings. Verify environmental limits and redundancy.

prompt: What should be prepared before a risky configuration change?
explanation: Maintain physical and logical diagrams, IPAM, inventories, baselines and configuration backups. Changes require impact analysis, approval, validation and rollback planning. Track end-of-life and end-of-support separately.

prompt: Which tool provides packet-level protocol fields for analysis?
explanation: SNMP polls counters and receives notifications; syslog records events; flow telemetry summarizes conversations; packet captures show packet detail. Baselines distinguish normal variation from anomalies. SIEM correlates logs across sources.

prompt: Which metric specifies acceptable data loss in time?
explanation: RPO is acceptable data loss measured in time; RTO is the target restoration time. Hot sites are more ready than cold sites. Redundancy reduces single points of failure but does not replace backups. Test recovery plans and validate restored services.

prompt: Which DNS record maps a hostname to IPv6?
explanation: DHCPv4 uses Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge. Relays forward requests across routed boundaries. DNS A and AAAA records map names to IPv4 and IPv6; PTR supports reverse lookup. NTP synchronizes clocks. IPv6 SLAAC uses router advertisements.

prompt: Which approach allows management when the production network is down?
explanation: SSH protects remote CLI sessions; HTTPS protects web management. Out-of-band management uses a separate access path. VPNs provide protected tunnels; split tunneling routes only selected traffic through them. Restrict management access to authorized networks.

prompt: Which AAA function determines permitted actions?
explanation: Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure; integrity protects correctness; availability keeps services usable. Authentication establishes identity, authorization grants access, accounting records activity. PKI binds identities to public keys using certificates. Least privilege limits access.

prompt: Which attack associates a gateway IP with an unauthorized MAC address?
explanation: ARP spoofing can redirect local traffic; rogue DHCP can supply false settings; DNS poisoning corrupts name resolution. DDoS exhausts resources; social engineering targets people. Investigate anomalies with logs and packet evidence; use segmentation and validated controls.

prompt: Which standard provides port-based network access authentication?
explanation: Disable unused services and ports, patch devices, restrict management, use ACLs and segmentation. 802.1X authenticates network access using a supplicant, authenticator and authentication server. MAC filtering alone is weak because addresses can be spoofed.

prompt: After a theory is confirmed, what comes next?
explanation: Identify the problem, establish a theory, test it, plan a solution, implement or escalate, verify functionality and preventive measures, document outcomes. If testing disproves a theory, establish a new one. Assess change impact before implementation.

prompt: Which tool measures received optical signal power?
explanation: Check link state, cable seating, interface counters, speed and duplex, optics and power. CRC errors may indicate physical corruption. A cable certifier validates standards; a toner traces copper; an optical power meter measures received light.

prompt: A DHCP client self-assigns 169.254.12.4. What should be investigated first?
explanation: Check VLAN membership, trunk allowances, STP state, IP address, mask, gateway and route table. Duplicate addresses cause intermittent reachability. APIPA suggests a DHCP failure or unavailable server. Isolate scope before changing configuration.

prompt: Which metric most directly describes variation in packet arrival delay?
explanation: Latency measures delay; jitter measures variation in delay; loss measures missing packets; throughput measures achieved rate. Congestion, interference and retransmissions reduce performance. Compare counters and measurements with baselines.

prompt: Which command directly queries DNS records?
explanation: Ping tests ICMP reachability; traceroute reveals responding hops; nslookup or dig queries DNS; ipconfig or ip displays addressing; netstat or ss shows sockets. Cisco show interfaces reveals counters; show ip route shows routes. Use scanners only on authorized systems.

prompt: Voice packets arrive with delays varying from 10 to 110 ms despite negligible loss. Which metric is the issue?
explanation: Jitter measures variation in packet delay and can disrupt real-time audio.

prompt: Which statement accurately describes Latency?
options: Elapsed time for data to travel between points
Offered traffic exceeds available forwarding capacity
Nearby wireless channels share spectrum and interfere
explanation: Latency refers to elapsed time for data to travel between points. The alternatives instead describe Congestion, Throughput, Channel overlap.

prompt: Which statement accurately describes Throughput?
options: Offered traffic exceeds available forwarding capacity
Elapsed time for data to travel between points
Nearby wireless channels share spectrum and interfere
explanation: Throughput refers to actual achieved data transfer rate. The alternatives instead describe Congestion, Latency, Channel overlap.

prompt: Which statement accurately describes Channel overlap?
options: Nearby wireless channels share spectrum and interfere
Offered traffic exceeds available forwarding capacity
Elapsed time for data to travel between points
explanation: Channel overlap refers to nearby wireless channels share spectrum and interfere. The alternatives instead describe Congestion, Latency, Throughput.

prompt: A Windows host reaches a server by IP but not by hostname. Which tool directly tests DNS resolution?
explanation: nslookup queries DNS and helps distinguish name resolution from basic IP reachability.

prompt: Which statement accurately describes Visual fault locator?
options: Visible light helps locate breaks or bends in fiber
Traces an unidentified copper cable to its termination
Inspect learned MAC addresses and associated switch ports on Cisco IOS
Capture and inspect packets from a command-line interface
explanation: Visual fault locator refers to visible light helps locate breaks or bends in fiber. The alternatives instead describe Toner, show mac address-table, tcpdump.

Traces an unidentified copper cable to its termination
Visible light helps locate breaks or bends in fiber
Capture and inspect packets from a command-line interface
explanation: show mac address-table refers to inspect learned MAC addresses and associated switch ports on Cisco IOS. The alternatives instead describe Toner, Visual fault locator, tcpdump.

options: Capture and inspect packets from a command-line interface
Traces an unidentified copper cable to its termination
Visible light helps locate breaks or bends in fiber
Inspect learned MAC addresses and associated switch ports on Cisco IOS

prompt: A capture shows valid Ethernet frames but TCP retransmissions after a remote firewall change. Which layer should you investigate for blocked destination ports?
explanation: TCP ports are transport-layer identifiers; valid frames do not establish end-to-end delivery. Physical and data link concern local transmission; presentation concerns representation.

prompt: A web service needs requests distributed among three healthy backend servers. Which component directly provides this function?
explanation: A load balancer selects backend servers; NAS provides file storage, a relay forwards DHCP, and an access switch forwards local frames.

prompt: Private cloud instances need outbound internet access without accepting unsolicited inbound connections. Which gateway is appropriate?
explanation: A NAT gateway translates outbound connections and permits return traffic; DNS resolves names, a circuit provides connectivity, and a bridge forwards frames.

prompt: A firewall allows UDP 53 but blocks TCP 53. Small DNS replies work while some large replies fail. What should be allowed?
explanation: DNS can retry truncated UDP replies over TCP 53. The other ports serve mail, DHCP and SMB respectively.

prompt: A campus link crosses a high-interference industrial area over 2 km. Which medium is most appropriate?
explanation: Single-mode fiber supports long optical links and resists electromagnetic interference. DAC and copper Ethernet have much shorter typical reach; USB is not a campus backbone medium.

prompt: A data center needs predictable paths between server racks with substantial east-west traffic. Which architecture fits?
explanation: Spine-leaf provides multiple paths and consistent hop counts between racks; the alternatives lack comparable fabric scalability.

prompt: A host has address 192.0.2.77/27. Which is its network address?
explanation: A /27 has blocks of 32; 77 falls in 64–95. The other boundaries are different subnets and 77 is a host address.

prompt: An IPv6-only client must reach an IPv4-only server through a translation service. Which technology addresses this?
explanation: NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4. LACP aggregates links, STP prevents bridging loops, and 802.1X controls access.

prompt: A routing table has 198.51.100.0/24 and 198.51.100.128/25. Which prefix matches 198.51.100.200 most specifically?
explanation: Longest prefix match selects /25; /24 is less specific and default is least specific.

prompt: Two switches carry VLANs 10 and 20 across one link, but VLAN 20 is absent from the allowed list. What change restores that VLAN?
explanation: The trunk must permit VLAN 20. Moving hosts changes segmentation, disabling STP risks loops, and DNS is unrelated.

prompt: An office has three nearby 2.4 GHz APs using 20 MHz channels in the US. Which plan minimizes mutual overlap?
explanation: Channels 1, 6 and 11 are the conventional non-overlapping plan; adjacent channels overlap and identical channels contend.

prompt: A rack must keep switches running during a brief utility outage. Which device provides temporary power?
explanation: A UPS supplies stored energy; a basic PDU distributes power and the other devices organize cabling.

prompt: A firmware update breaks connectivity. Which artifact best supports restoration of the prior settings?
explanation: A configuration backup preserves settings; the other documents describe assets, coverage or physical placement.

prompt: An analyst needs to identify which endpoints consume the most bandwidth without recording payloads. Which source is best?
explanation: Flow records summarize endpoints and byte counts; payload capture is unnecessary, and diagrams and zone files do not measure traffic.

prompt: Backups occur every four hours and recovery takes 45 minutes. Which metric describes the potential four-hour data loss window?
explanation: RPO concerns recoverable data age; RTO concerns restoration time, MTTR repair time and MTBF reliability intervals.

prompt: A mail administrator needs DNS to identify the receiving mail servers for a domain. Which record is appropriate?
explanation: MX specifies mail exchangers; PTR supports reverse lookup, AAAA stores IPv6 addresses and CNAME aliases names.

prompt: A router loses its production network connection but its console server is reachable on a separate management network. Which method is this?
explanation: The separate management path is out-of-band; in-band shares production connectivity, split tunneling selects VPN routes and mirroring copies traffic.

prompt: A help desk employee should reset passwords but not modify firewall policies. Which principle directly limits permissions?
explanation: Least privilege limits access to required duties; locality concerns data location, availability service access and geofencing geographic conditions.

prompt: A workstation receives false gateway MAC mappings from another LAN host. Which attack best explains this?
explanation: ARP poisoning falsifies IPv4-to-MAC mappings; the alternatives target DNS data, radio availability or credentials.

prompt: Guest devices must reach the internet but never internal file servers. Which design best enforces this?
options: Separate guest VLAN with restrictive firewall policy
Shared VLAN with a different SSID only
explanation: Segmentation plus enforced policy limits paths; SSID alone need not isolate traffic, and logging or leases do not enforce access.

prompt: A technician suspects a damaged patch cable. Before replacing a switch, what should happen next?
options: Test the cable hypothesis with a known-good cable
explanation: A controlled test verifies the suspected cause before broader changes; the alternatives are premature or disruptive.

prompt: A copper link negotiates at 100 Mbps instead of 1 Gbps after a cable replacement. Which test is most useful first?
options: Verify all four wire pairs with a cable tester
explanation: Gigabit copper Ethernet requires four pairs; a wire-map test can reveal faults. DNS, routing and time do not determine physical negotiation.

prompt: A host reaches peers in its own subnet but cannot reach any remote subnet. Its configured gateway is outside its local prefix. What should be corrected?
explanation: A conventional gateway must be reachable on the local link; the other settings do not repair next-hop reachability.

prompt: A WAN link reaches capacity during backups and voice delay rises. Which change most directly protects voice during congestion?
explanation: QoS schedules delay-sensitive traffic preferentially; the alternatives do not control congested queues.

prompt: A Windows client resolves a hostname but TCP 443 connections fail. Which command directly tests that destination port?
explanation: Test-NetConnection can test TCP reachability; ipconfig displays settings, arp displays neighbor mappings and hostname identifies the local system.
